controls.name: Policies for information security
controls.why: Policies give every other control its authority.
controls.how: Top-level policy approved by the CEO on 19 February 2027 and eleven topic policies approved by 23 April 2027. All are published in Confluence.
controls.first_ev: Approved policy set with version history

controls.name: Information security roles and responsibilities
controls.why: The gap assessment found controls that nobody owned.
controls.how: RACI published in the ISMS Manual. Every control in this statement has a named owner, and the CISO reports to the CEO.
controls.first_ev: ISMS Manual, RACI and control owner list

controls.name: Segregation of duties
controls.why: One person could write, approve and release a change or a payout file.
controls.how: A second approver is enforced in CI for 97% of production deployments. Dual approval of payout files is being configured with Vaskora Bank.
controls.first_ev: Deployment log, change approvals and security gate records

controls.name: Management responsibilities
controls.why: Policies fail unless line managers enforce them.
controls.how: Security duties are part of manager responsibilities. Managers confirm training and asset return.
controls.first_ev: ISMS Manual, RACI and control owner list

controls.name: Contact with authorities
controls.why: Orvanta must reach its supervisor and the data protection authority quickly during an incident.
controls.how: The Head of Compliance holds the contact list, which the incident plan references. It is checked every quarter.
controls.first_ev: Legal register and authority contact list

controls.name: Contact with special interest groups
controls.why: A small security team needs outside warning of sector threats.
controls.how: Orvanta joined a financial-sector sharing group in March 2027, and the CISO attends its monthly calls.
controls.first_ev: Threat intelligence review notes and sharing group membership

controls.name: Threat intelligence
controls.why: A threat-informed risk assessment depends on current threat information.
controls.how: A monthly threat review updates the threat catalog. Mapping intelligence to SIEM detections follows the SIEM rollout.
controls.first_ev: Threat intelligence review notes and sharing group membership

controls.name: Information security in project management
controls.why: New features changed data handling without security input.
controls.how: A security check sits in the Jira project template, at the start and before launch.
controls.first_ev: ISMS steering minutes, KPI dashboard and control test calendar

controls.name: Inventory of information and other associated assets
controls.why: The gap assessment found 43 unmanaged laptops and SaaS tools with no owner.
controls.how: A single asset register has been live since March 2027 and is reconciled monthly against Terraform, Jamf and Okta.
controls.first_ev: Asset register and device lifecycle records

controls.name: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
controls.why: Staff need clear rules for systems, data and AI tools.
controls.how: Acceptable Use Policy approved. All staff acknowledged it at rollout, and joiners acknowledge it on day one.
controls.first_ev: Approved policy set with version history

controls.name: Return of assets
controls.why: Three of 18 sampled leavers had no asset return record.
controls.how: Asset return is a tracked step in the leaver procedure, confirmed by the line manager.
controls.first_ev: Joiner, mover and leaver tickets with timestamps

controls.name: Classification of information
controls.why: Card numbers and identity documents had spread into tickets and chat.
controls.how: A four-level scheme is published, and all 26 systems and nine data classes are mapped to it.
controls.first_ev: Classification scheme, labels and retention schedule

controls.name: Labelling of information
controls.why: Labels make handling rules visible where sensitive data lives.
controls.how: Shared drives holding Restricted information are labelled. Confidential drives are being labelled.
controls.first_ev: Classification scheme, labels and retention schedule

controls.name: Information transfer
controls.why: Personal data is viewed from Baku, outside the EEA.
controls.how: Transfer rules are in policy. The transfer impact assessment is in DPO review.
controls.first_ev: Record of processing and transfer impact assessment

controls.name: Access control
controls.why: Excess access turns one stolen account into a full compromise.
controls.how: Role groups in Okta define standard access, and system owners approve anything beyond them.
controls.first_ev: Okta application, MFA and device trust reports

controls.name: Identity management
controls.why: Shared admin accounts hid who had acted.
controls.how: Every workforce identity is named in Okta. Two of three shared admin accounts are gone, and the last one goes when the legacy AWS account is retired.
controls.first_ev: Okta and AWS administrator role reports

controls.name: Authentication information
controls.why: Long-lived AWS keys sat in nine repositories.
controls.how: The password manager is mandatory and security keys are issued. Pipelines are finishing the move to short-lived OIDC roles.
controls.first_ev: Key inventory and secrets configuration

controls.name: Access rights
controls.why: Leaver access lasted a median of nine days.
controls.how: Deprovisioning is automated from Personio to Okta, with a median suspension time of 20 hours. The first quarterly review is complete.
controls.first_ev: Joiner, mover and leaver tickets with timestamps

controls.name: Information security in supplier relationships
controls.why: Five critical services are outsourced, and none had been assessed.
controls.how: Supplier Security Policy approved and 20 vendors tiered. Three of eight Tier 1 suppliers are assessed.
controls.first_ev: Third-party risk register and supplier assessments

controls.name: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
controls.why: Contracts lacked consistent security, audit and notification clauses.
controls.how: The contract checklist is used for new contracts. Tier 1 contracts are updated as they renew.
controls.first_ev: Supplier contracts, NDAs and contract checklist

controls.name: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
controls.why: Software dependencies and suppliers' own suppliers were unknown.
controls.how: Software bills of materials are generated in CI. Subprocessor lists have been requested from Tier 1 suppliers.
controls.first_ev: Branch protection, scanning and SBOM settings

controls.name: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
controls.why: Supplier assurance must not lapse unnoticed.
controls.how: The yearly review cycle starts once the first Tier 1 assessments finish. Expiry tracking is set up in the register.
controls.first_ev: Third-party risk register and supplier assessments

controls.name: Information security for use of cloud services
controls.why: All production runs in AWS.
controls.how: A cloud security standard and shared responsibility matrix are drafted. Exit considerations follow the BIA.
controls.first_ev: Terraform repository, architecture standards and runbooks

controls.name: Information security incident management planning and preparation
controls.why: The 2023 draft plan had never been exercised.
controls.how: The plan, on-call rota and two playbooks were approved in April 2027. The first tabletop exercise is scheduled.
controls.first_ev: Incident plan, playbooks, severity matrix and incident records

controls.name: Assessment and decision on information security events
controls.why: On-call engineers decided case by case.
controls.how: A severity matrix is in use and feeds the classification needed for regulatory reporting.
controls.first_ev: Incident plan, playbooks, severity matrix and incident records

controls.name: Response to information security incidents
controls.why: Response worked for outages but was untested for attacks.
controls.how: Roles and authority are defined. Effectiveness stays unproven until the tabletop exercise.
controls.first_ev: Incident plan, playbooks, severity matrix and incident records

controls.name: Learning from information security incidents
controls.why: Security events were not reviewed afterwards.
controls.how: Post-incident reviews now cover security events, with actions tracked in Jira.
controls.first_ev: Incident plan, playbooks, severity matrix and incident records

controls.name: Collection of evidence
controls.why: No procedure existed for preserving evidence.
controls.how: An evidence handling procedure is drafted, and security logs are kept for 12 months.
controls.first_ev: Incident plan, playbooks, severity matrix and incident records

controls.name: Information security during disruption
controls.why: A crisis invites security shortcuts.
controls.how: The requirement is set in the Backup and Recovery Policy. Detailed rules follow the continuity plan.
controls.first_ev: Business Impact Analysis and continuity plan

controls.name: ICT readiness for business continuity
controls.why: No recovery objectives had been set.
controls.how: The BIA is in progress and restore tests prove database recovery. A failover exercise is planned.
controls.first_ev: Business Impact Analysis and continuity plan

controls.name: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
controls.why: Orvanta is a regulated payment institution.
controls.how: An obligations list exists. It is being extended into a full legal register with owners.
controls.first_ev: Legal register and authority contact list

controls.name: Intellectual property rights
controls.why: Open-source license terms apply to the code Orvanta ships.
controls.how: License scanning runs in CI, and the General Counsel manages commercial licenses.
controls.first_ev: Branch protection, scanning and SBOM settings

controls.name: Protection of records
controls.why: Ledger and AML records must be kept, and other records deleted on time.
controls.how: A single retention schedule was published in March 2027.
controls.first_ev: Classification scheme, labels and retention schedule

controls.name: Privacy and protection of PII
controls.why: Orvanta is a controller of customer and staff personal data.
controls.how: A DPO and a record of processing are in place. Safeguards for Baku access await the transfer assessment.
controls.first_ev: Record of processing and transfer impact assessment

controls.name: Independent review of information security
controls.why: Certification needs an independent review of the ISMS.
controls.how: The internal audit programme is approved, and the first full audit is planned for July 2027.
controls.first_ev: ISMS steering minutes, KPI dashboard and control test calendar

controls.name: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
controls.why: Controls decay unless someone tests them.
controls.how: A control testing calendar is set and its first cycle is running.
controls.first_ev: ISMS steering minutes, KPI dashboard and control test calendar

controls.name: Documented operating procedures
controls.why: Operating knowledge sat in people's heads.
controls.how: Runbooks for backup, access and incident tasks are standardized. Other SRE runbooks are in progress.
controls.first_ev: Terraform repository, architecture standards and runbooks

controls.name: Screening
controls.why: People in privileged roles can move money and data.
controls.how: Identity, right-to-work and reference checks cover all hires. Privileged and finance roles get further checks where the law allows.
controls.first_ev: Screening, contract and disciplinary records

controls.name: Terms and conditions of employment
controls.why: Contracts make security duties binding.
controls.how: The Vilnius and Baku templates were aligned in March 2027.
controls.first_ev: Screening, contract and disciplinary records

controls.name: Information security awareness, education and training
controls.why: Phishing is the first step in two of the three attack scenarios.
controls.how: Role-based training stands at 96% completion. The first phishing simulation ran in April 2027, with an 11% click rate.
controls.first_ev: Training, acknowledgment and phishing simulation records

controls.name: Disciplinary process
controls.why: A policy needs a fair consequence.
controls.how: The disciplinary process names security breaches and protects good-faith reporting.
controls.first_ev: Screening, contract and disciplinary records

controls.name: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
controls.why: Movers kept access from their old roles.
controls.how: HR notifies IT Operations the same day, and leavers get an exit reminder of their duties.
controls.first_ev: Joiner, mover and leaver tickets with timestamps

controls.name: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
controls.why: Contractors and suppliers see Confidential information.
controls.how: NDAs are signed before access, and the template is reviewed every two years.
controls.first_ev: Screening, contract and disciplinary records

controls.name: Remote working
controls.why: Most staff work remotely.
controls.how: Remote Working Policy approved. All laptops are enrolled, and Okta blocks unmanaged devices.
controls.first_ev: Jamf compliance report: enrollment, encryption, lock, USB, DNS filter

controls.name: Information security event reporting
controls.why: Staff had no defined way to report an event.
controls.how: The #security-report channel and the phishing report button have been live since January 2027.
controls.first_ev: Incident plan, playbooks, severity matrix and incident records

controls.name: Physical security perimeters
controls.why: Offices hold staff devices and network equipment.
controls.how: Office perimeters are recorded in the ISMS scope.
controls.first_ev: Office walkthrough records and visitor logs

controls.name: Physical entry
controls.why: Visitors enter both offices.
controls.how: Badge entry in Vilnius, reception control in Baku and a visitor log in both.
controls.first_ev: Office walkthrough records and visitor logs

controls.name: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
controls.why: Offices must be secure out of hours.
controls.how: Offices are locked out of hours, and this is checked yearly.
controls.first_ev: Office walkthrough records and visitor logs

controls.name: Physical security monitoring
controls.why: Entry to the offices must be observable.
controls.how: CCTV covers Vilnius entrances. The landlord's monitoring is confirmed for Baku.
controls.first_ev: Office walkthrough records and visitor logs

controls.name: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
controls.why: Production depends on AWS facilities.
controls.how: The CISO reviews AWS assurance reports every year.
controls.first_ev: AWS assurance reports and yearly review note

controls.name: Working in secure areas
controls.why: No Orvanta office holds production systems or a restricted work area, so there are no secure areas to control. The exclusion is reassessed if that changes (requirement IS-23).
controls.how: Not applicable.

controls.name: Clear desk and clear screen
controls.why: Shared and home workspaces expose screens and papers.
controls.how: Screen lock is enforced through Jamf, and the clear desk rule is in the Acceptable Use Policy.
controls.first_ev: Jamf compliance report: enrollment, encryption, lock, USB, DNS filter

controls.name: Equipment siting and protection
controls.why: Office network equipment needs physical protection.
controls.how: Network equipment sits in locked cabinets.
controls.first_ev: Office walkthrough records and visitor logs

controls.name: Security of assets off-premises
controls.why: Laptops travel with a remote workforce.
controls.how: Disk encryption and remote wipe are enforced on all 131 laptops.
controls.first_ev: Jamf compliance report: enrollment, encryption, lock, USB, DNS filter

controls.name: Storage media
controls.why: An insider could copy data to USB storage.
controls.how: Jamf blocks removable storage for roles that handle Restricted information.
controls.first_ev: Jamf compliance report: enrollment, encryption, lock, USB, DNS filter

controls.name: Supporting utilities
controls.why: Production utilities are inherited from AWS.
controls.how: Covered by AWS assurance. Offices have basic backup power.
controls.first_ev: AWS assurance reports and yearly review note

controls.name: Cabling security
controls.why: Office cabling is limited but carries staff traffic.
controls.how: Cabling runs in locked areas.
controls.first_ev: Office walkthrough records and visitor logs

controls.name: Equipment maintenance
controls.why: A repair can expose data on a device.
controls.how: Repairs go only through IT Operations.
controls.first_ev: Asset register and device lifecycle records

controls.name: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
controls.why: Old laptops can leak data.
controls.how: Wipe evidence is recorded in Jamf. A disposal supplier that issues certificates is being contracted.
controls.first_ev: Asset register and device lifecycle records

controls.name: User endpoint devices
controls.why: One unmanaged engineer laptop was enough to steal cloud sessions.
controls.how: All 131 laptops are enrolled in Jamf, and Okta blocks unmanaged devices.
controls.first_ev: Jamf compliance report: enrollment, encryption, lock, USB, DNS filter

controls.name: Privileged access rights
controls.why: One stolen admin session gave control of production.
controls.how: Just-in-time access is live for AWS and Kubernetes, and super admins are cut to two. One shared admin remains in the legacy account.
controls.first_ev: Just-in-time access request and session logs

controls.name: Information access restriction
controls.why: Engineers could read production personal data broadly.
controls.how: Access to S3 and databases is restricted by role. Masking by default is being rolled out.
controls.first_ev: Just-in-time access request and session logs

controls.name: Access to source code
controls.why: Unprotected repositories let code be changed quietly.
controls.how: Branch protection covers all production repositories.
controls.first_ev: Branch protection, scanning and SBOM settings

controls.name: Secure authentication
controls.why: Five tools sat outside MFA.
controls.how: All workforce tools are behind Okta MFA, administrators use security keys and OpenVPN is replaced.
controls.first_ev: Okta application, MFA and device trust reports

controls.name: Capacity management
controls.why: Payment availability depends on capacity.
controls.how: Autoscaling and capacity dashboards are monitored, with a yearly forecast.
controls.first_ev: Terraform repository, architecture standards and runbooks

controls.name: Protection against malware
controls.why: Malware on a laptop starts two of the attack scenarios.
controls.how: EDR runs on all laptops and reports to the SIEM. Container images are scanned in CI.
controls.first_ev: EDR coverage and alert report

controls.name: Management of technical vulnerabilities
controls.why: Legacy hosts lagged on patches.
controls.how: Severity deadlines are adopted and tracked. The legacy EC2 hosts are being retired.
controls.first_ev: Vulnerability dashboard and remediation tickets

controls.name: Configuration management
controls.why: Manual changes hide drift and backdoors.
controls.how: Terraform is applied only from CI. Drift alerting is being tuned.
controls.first_ev: Terraform repository, architecture standards and runbooks

controls.name: Information deletion
controls.why: Card numbers were found in support tickets.
controls.how: Tickets are purged and redacted. Automated deletion against the retention schedule is in progress.
controls.first_ev: Ticket redaction settings, monthly search results and masking configuration

controls.name: Data masking
controls.why: Reporting and support views showed full personal data.
controls.how: Card numbers are truncated everywhere. Masking in Metabase and Orbit is in rollout.
controls.first_ev: Ticket redaction settings, monthly search results and masking configuration

controls.name: Data leakage prevention
controls.why: Bulk exports raised no alert.
controls.how: Workspace DLP rules and export alerts are designed and scheduled.
controls.first_ev: SIEM source inventory, detection rules and triage log

controls.name: Information backup
controls.why: Backups shared the production account and had never been restored.
controls.how: Backups sit in an isolated, immutable account with a copy in a second region. Two quarterly restore tests have passed.
controls.first_ev: Backup configuration and restore test records

controls.name: Redundancy of information processing facilities
controls.why: Payments must survive the loss of a data center.
controls.how: Services run across three availability zones. The single-region risk is accepted under RA-01.
controls.first_ev: Terraform repository, architecture standards and runbooks

controls.name: Logging
controls.why: CloudTrail was off in one AWS account.
controls.how: Organization-wide trails feed a protected log account, with 12-month retention.
controls.first_ev: Organization trail and log account configuration

controls.name: Monitoring activities
controls.why: Nobody was watching the logs.
controls.how: The SIEM is live with 40% of priority sources and daily triage. The remaining sources are due by June.
controls.first_ev: SIEM source inventory, detection rules and triage log

controls.name: Clock synchronization
controls.why: Investigations need consistent timestamps.
controls.how: AWS time synchronization is used across services.
controls.first_ev: Organization trail and log account configuration

controls.name: Use of privileged utility programs
controls.why: Administrative tools were open to all engineers.
controls.how: Tools are limited to approved roles. Session recording is in rollout.
controls.first_ev: Just-in-time access request and session logs

controls.name: Installation of software on operational systems
controls.why: Legacy hosts accepted manual installs.
controls.how: Production runs from built images. Manual access ends when the legacy hosts retire.
controls.first_ev: Terraform repository, architecture standards and runbooks

controls.name: Networks security
controls.why: A shared VPN profile reached the database subnets.
controls.how: Identity-aware access replaced OpenVPN in March 2027.
controls.first_ev: Terraform repository, architecture standards and runbooks

controls.name: Security of network services
controls.why: Edge and load-balancer settings protect the payment API.
controls.how: Required settings are documented and checked in code review.
controls.first_ev: Terraform repository, architecture standards and runbooks

controls.name: Segregation of networks
controls.why: Broad peering linked the legacy account to production.
controls.how: Peering is restricted, and the legacy account is being retired.
controls.first_ev: Terraform repository, architecture standards and runbooks

controls.name: Web filtering
controls.why: Staff could reach phishing and malware sites.
controls.how: DNS filtering runs on all managed laptops.
controls.first_ev: Jamf compliance report: enrollment, encryption, lock, USB, DNS filter

controls.name: Use of cryptography
controls.why: Customer and payment data must stay unreadable if stolen.
controls.how: KMS encryption at rest, TLS 1.2 or higher in transit, and a key inventory with a rotation schedule.
controls.first_ev: Key inventory and secrets configuration

controls.name: Secure development life cycle
controls.why: Security gates in delivery were undefined.
controls.how: A life cycle with gates by risk tier is published. Teams are adopting it.
controls.first_ev: Deployment log, change approvals and security gate records

controls.name: Application security requirements
controls.why: Abuse cases for the payment API were rarely considered.
controls.how: A requirement baseline for payment and API changes is published and used for new work.
controls.first_ev: Deployment log, change approvals and security gate records

controls.name: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
controls.why: Design rules were unwritten.
controls.how: Engineering principles are published, and threat modeling has started for major changes.
controls.first_ev: Deployment log, change approvals and security gate records

controls.name: Secure coding
controls.why: Code scanning covered few repositories.
controls.how: Static, dependency and secret scanning run on production repositories. Other repositories are in progress.
controls.first_ev: Branch protection, scanning and SBOM settings

controls.name: Security testing in development and acceptance
controls.why: Security testing was limited to one test a year.
controls.how: The yearly penetration test continues. Dynamic testing in staging is being added.
controls.first_ev: Penetration test report and test scoping records

controls.name: Outsourced development
controls.why: Orvanta does not outsource software development, as the CTO confirmed. Baku is an in-group team under the same life cycle. The exclusion is reassessed if outsourcing starts (requirement SD-06).
controls.how: Not applicable.

controls.name: Separation of development, test and production environments
controls.why: Environments must not share risk.
controls.how: Separate AWS accounts are in use, and standing production access is removed.
controls.first_ev: Terraform repository, architecture standards and runbooks

controls.name: Change management
controls.why: 14% of deployments bypassed review.
controls.how: The CI path is enforced for 97% of production deployments. The last Jenkins jobs are being migrated.
controls.first_ev: Deployment log, change approvals and security gate records

controls.name: Test information
controls.why: A team used live samples in staging.
controls.how: Policy bans live data in test. Automated masking is in progress.
controls.first_ev: Ticket redaction settings, monthly search results and masking configuration

controls.name: Protection of information systems during audit testing
controls.why: Testing can disrupt payments.
controls.how: Tests are scoped and scheduled with the Head of Platform and SRE.
controls.first_ev: Penetration test report and test scoping records
